message: Can you look at this ECG? I think it's normal, right?
reply:
**I would not call this ECG normal.** The rhythm appears regular, around 60 beats/minute, but there is **ST elevation across several chest leads, especially V2–V5**, with abnormal loss of the usual upward R waves.

This pattern is concerning for an **anterior heart attack**. An older heart attack can sometimes produce persistent changes, but a photo alone cannot distinguish these safely. ST elevation in adjacent leads warrants urgent assessment in the appropriate clinical setting. [ESC guidelines](https://academic.oup.com/eurheartj/article/44/38/3720/7243210)

**If you have chest discomfort, breathlessness, sweating, nausea, or faintness now, call emergency services immediately and do not drive yourself.** If this ECG was just recorded, get immediate medical review even if you feel well; comparison with older ECGs and blood troponin testing may be needed.

When was this recorded, and are you having any symptoms?
